intelligence.human_view: This is "eat our own cooking" (SN-3222) given its order — and the order is the teaching. Most teams write the manual first and then discover the system doesn't work the way the manual says. He reverses it: operate it yourself first, until you know it cold, then help others operate it, and only then write the manual — because the manual has to come from what actually worked, not from what was designed. The middle step is the one that gets skipped: "use it now" and "consistently using it" are not a launch event, they are a habit — everything in there, operational, every day. A vault completed but never used is a museum; a manual written before operating is a guess. The gap-fix round closed G1–G6 at 02:16Z with proof, so the door is built; the open step is not another build, it is the using. That is also why the sequence starts with the smart note: the teaching goes into the system first, so the operating is already the system teaching itself.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you build a clubhouse and then you write the rule book before anyone has ever played in it — the rules would be all wrong. Shawn says: build the clubhouse, play in it yourself every day until you know every corner, help your friends play in it too — and THEN write the rule book, from what actually worked.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn says: write the note into the system, finish the vault, and then use it, dear — really use it, every day, everything in there, working properly. You have to operate it yourself first, dear, so you know it cold — then you can help others operate it — and only then do you write the manual for everyone, dear, because the manual has to come from what actually worked, not from a guess.
intelligence.naya_view: COMPLETE THE VAULT — OPERATE IT, THEN WRITE THE MANUAL. USE IT NOW, EVERYTHING IN THERE, OPERATIONAL, USED CONSISTENTLY. OPERATE IT YOURSELF FIRST, THEN HELP OTHERS, THEN WRITE THE MANUAL.
